analysis: The PR is documentation-only: it adds docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md and one index line plus a date bump in docs/reports/README.md. No executable code, protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage logic changes, so no control in TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 or TB-011 is weakened. The report describes prefill geometry measurements. It says Gemma 4 takes 2,048/4,096 by default, while GPT-OSS and dense Qwen keep 512/2,048 with an env opt-in. It also describes an unmerged-from-this-PR media ceiling and an activation-memory margin analysis. The security-relevant claims concern availability and memory pressure. The report states that at 32k with eight rows the wide geometry puts GPT-OSS and Qwen3.5-9B activation 0.12 and 0.53 GiB beyond their floors, which is why those models are not defaulted; the document itself acknowledges this. It also notes that the 512/2,048 arms lost rows to the 120 s admission lease, and that the p99 and max inter-token latency grow under the wide geometry. Those are performance and DoS-adjacent observations (T-029, T-010 area), not regressions introduced by this PR. The behavior the document describes (defaults, media ceiling, UnifiedMemoryCap, DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* env vars) lives in code outside this PR, so I could not verify it. If the corresponding code change lands separately, a later review should check whether the new default raises activation peaks beyond the memory cap for Gemma on small Macs (16-24 GB were not measured, per the limitations). The report does not touch the cache threat T-041 beyond the statement that no load arm used repeated prefixes. README.md retained links are unchanged.
